findings.english_quote: We retain the ancient time reference; explanatory footnote gives modern equivalent.
findings.issue: The lexical rationale inaccurately describes the supplied footnote. Footnote 1 gives no modern equivalent and explicitly says that the source gives no modern clock time. This leaves the decision metadata contradicting the reader-facing disclosure.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the rationale to describe the actual decision, for example: “We retain the ancient ordinal time reference; the footnote discloses the reported fifth/sixth-hour variation without assigning a modern clock time.” Review this proposed metadata replacement before adoption.

findings.issue: The lexical_decisions chosen value does not match the supplied translation, which reads “do their works.” Consequently, the audit metadata records a rendering that this edition does not use. This is a documentation defect, not a reason to substitute “deeds” into the translation.
findings.suggested_revision: Align the chosen value with the actual text, “do their works,” and review the accompanying rationale against that wording, including its treatment of the source's verb/noun wording pattern. Any proposed textual replacement requires a separate source review.

findings.english_quote: We retain the ancient time reference; explanatory footnote gives modern equivalent.
findings.issue: The simplified edition independently contains the same inaccurate description of its footnote. Its footnote 1 does not supply a modern equivalent and expressly declines to assign a modern clock time. The metadata therefore contradicts this edition's actual disclosure.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the rationale to describe retention of the ancient ordinal and disclosure of the reported fifth/sixth-hour variation without a modern clock conversion. Review the replacement metadata before adoption.

findings.issue: The simplified edition's lexical_decisions chosen value records “do their deeds,” but its own translation reads “do their works.” The metadata is not an accurate account of this edition's rendering.
findings.suggested_revision: Align the chosen value with this edition's actual wording, “do their works,” and freshly review the rationale's account of the Greek verb/noun pattern. Do not automatically replace the reader text with the metadata wording.

summary: Both editions were independently compared with all nine selected Greek paragraphs. Their reader texts preserve the narrative clauses, speakers, names, negations, necessity, confession, household share, perseverance command, sitting promise, and works/endurance conditions. Revision is needed for two concrete metadata inconsistencies in each edition, not for a demonstrated main-text omission or doctrinal alteration. The variant notes are compatible with the supplied attributed reports and distinguish editorial supplements, conjecture, corrector layers, and mediated versional evidence. This review does not authenticate unseen images, certify the reported editions, or establish exhaustive collation.
